_comment: THE REPOSITORY, declared as an initialized instance. Owner, 2026-09-20: "only uploads/ on this repo's root b/c acting as if it was intialized" — this checkout is not merely the platform's source tree, it behaves as a folio that has been initialized, and an initialized instance's ingestion queue sits at ITS root. Before this, `uploads` was declared ONLY by cat-harness with instance scope, so the queue resolved to `cat-harness/uploads/` and the root had none. The obvious alternative — giving cat-harness's `uploads` entry `scope: "repository"` — was tried and MEASURED: 6 tests red, three of them the guarantee that a dependent instance inherits its own uploads/ and library/, two that the upload URL carries the instance segment. That is a real property and it is not being traded away, so the root gets its OWN declaration instead and cat-harness's is untouched.
name: folio-assistant
description: The repository itself, acting as an initialized instance. It declares the directories a person drops things into, which belong to the checkout rather than to any one layer inside it.

directories.description: The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline for THIS checkout — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. Distinct from `cat-harness/uploads/`, which is the harness layer's own queue: the two are different instances' directories that happen to share an id, not one directory declared twice. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus; a source sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk.
